example_input: The parser test in this repo is failing — find out why and fix it.
note: Every module link pins the exact commit this teardown is based on — xai-org/grok-build @ 2bdd1d6a6369, pinned by commit (the repository publishes no tags).

modules.label: AgentBuilder::build — the definition becomes a runnable Agent

steps.narrative: The session actor loads the agent definition — system prompt, project instructions, an allowlist/denylist-filtered tool list, an optional turn budget (unset for this run) — and folds in memory reminders. The prompt is sent to the loop, which lives in the ACP session implementation.
steps.title: Prompt assembly — the definition becomes the request

modules.label: run_turn_via_sampler — the loop's one model call
the sampler's stream layer — Chat Completions / Messages / Responses

steps.narrative: Iteration one. The loop calls the sampler exactly once — run_turn_via_sampler — and streams the reply. The wire format (Chat Completions, Messages, or Responses) comes from the model's catalog entry; this session's traffic is proxied, an API-key session would go to api.x.ai.
steps.title: Sampling — one round-trip per iteration

steps.narrative: The reply carries two tool calls: a grep for the failing test and a read_file on the parser. Before anything executes, the stationarity guard hashes this step's signature — tool name plus arguments, order-insensitive — and starts a run count. A fresh signature, so the run is 1.
steps.representation:
tool_calls: [
  grep(pattern: "test_parse_header"),
  read_file(path: "src/parser.rs"),
]
step signature: hash(tool name + args)  // order-insensitive
run count for this signature: 1
steps.title: Tool calls arrive — and get hashed

modules.label: the shipped guide — the same five steps, documented

steps.narrative: Each call walks the pipeline in order: PreToolUse hooks, merged rules (deny > ask > allow), remembered per-project grants, then the built-in read-only auto-approvals. grep and read_file are read-only — both approve here, per segment, with no prompt. The mode's policy step is never reached.
steps.representation:
check_tool(grep) ->
  hooks: no deny
  rules: no match
  grants: none
  read-only auto-approval: yes  => Allow
check_tool(read_file) -> same path => Allow
steps.title: Authorization — read-only calls approve themselves

modules.label: finalize_tool_calls — results fold back into the turn

steps.narrative: The workspace crate executes both calls against the real file system — ungated by any sandbox, because no --sandbox profile was given at startup. The results show the test's expectation and the parser code disagree about a header field. Both results are appended to the conversation.
steps.representation:
tool_result(grep):
  tests/parser_test.rs:88 — expects field `kind`
tool_result(read_file):
  src/parser.rs — parser emits field `type`
// appended to the conversation; the loop iterates
steps.title: Results return — the loop iterates

modules.label: permission/manager — the same pipeline, a different tier answers

steps.narrative: Iteration two: the model proposes search_replace to align the parser with the test. An edit is not read-only, so the pipeline falls through to the default mode's policy — a prompt. The user approves with 'always allow in this project', and the choice is stored as a per-project grant before the edit runs.
steps.representation:
check_tool(search_replace) ->
  hooks: no deny · rules: no match · grants: none
  read-only auto-approval: no (it writes)
  mode policy (default): Prompt
user: Allow + always allow in this project
  => grant stored (per-project, survives restarts)
steps.title: The edit prompts — and the grant is remembered

modules.label: bash_command_splitting.rs — chained commands split into segments
workspace_ops — the test run executes here

steps.narrative: The model verifies with a terminal run of the test suite. The command is authorized the same way — the fresh grant covers the prompt — and the permission layer checks the command per segment rather than as one string. The tests pass; the output joins the conversation.
steps.representation:
tool_call: run_terminal_command("cargo test parser")
  segments: [cargo test parser] — checked individually
  grant from step 6 covers the prompt => Allow
tool_result: test result: ok — 214 passed
steps.title: Verification — per-segment checks, tests pass

modules.label: resolve_trace_upload — the tier chain that decides

steps.narrative: Iteration three returns prose and no tool calls, so the turn ends — the classic exit condition. Turn-end runs trace completion: in this source tree the resolver's tiers all land on off (telemetry defaults to Disabled, and the trace default follows it), so nothing is packaged or sent. A deployment whose remote settings enable it would upload the turn here.
steps.representation:
reply: text only, tool_calls: []  => turn ends
complete_prompt_trace(turn):
  resolve_trace_upload() -> OFF in this tree
    (tiers: capability -> pin -> env -> config
     -> remote -> default = telemetry mode)
  => no manifest, no upload queue entry
steps.title: No tool calls — the turn ends, and the upload decision runs

title: One turn through Grok Build — step-by-step
